newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says small fire continues at Ca. plant.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says small fire continues at Ca. plant.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Monday a "very small" fire continued burning at the alkylation unit of its Wilmington, California, refinery following an early morning blaze which trimmed the plant's output.
"We have to keep it burning until the (left-over) fuel is out of the lines," said a plant spokeswoman.
The unit has a 9,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) capacity and helps make gasoline.
The company spokeswoman said she did not know when it would restart, but added an investigation was underway to determine the fire's cause.
She declined to say what the effect was on production. The plant's normal crude distillation capacity is 92,000 bpd.
Separately, plant officials continue to investigate the cause of a November fire at the facility's 20,000 bpd hydrotreating unit.
"We thought we'd have it up by now," the spokewoman said.

Wholesale gasoline prices jumped as much as 2.75 cents a gallon early after news of the fire. Later, they retreated on pressure from U.S. energy futures markets, West Coast petroleum products traders said.
